prompt_en: A documentary environmental photograph of water in several connected visible forms, organized as one coherent scene with linked causes and results. A person based visually on the supplied portrait is portrayed as a fictional boatyard worker. Use the attached image's visible face and short hairstyle, including the dark chin-length bob and fine parted fringe. She wears a faded ochre canvas work shirt with the cuffs turned back, dark work trousers and rubber boots, with a quietly appealing, natural face and a small look of concentration as she watches the water. At a small shoreline boatyard just after rain, an open varnished wooden dinghy rests firmly on two low cradles beside wet paving. The worker stands outside its near side, both boots planted on the paving and her torso leaning only slightly toward the gunwale. A compact manual bilge pump is fixed to the near gunwale within easy reach. Her right hand presses its short lever downward while her left palm steadies the rim, the two forearms visibly connected to their own shoulders. A clear intake hose curves into the shallow pool at the boat's lowest point, and a separate outlet hose curves over the near side with its open end held above a shallow ground puddle. The water is visibly moving and changing shape: a continuous liquid column arches down from the outlet hose into the shallow ground puddle. The hose mouth remains a visible source opening, physically joined to the descending water. The ground puddle is a coherent landing or receiving region, with a low fan of impact splash, individual spray droplets and concentric ripples radiating from that same landing point. Inside the dinghy, pale cloud reflections soften over the translucent bilge water while wooden seams remain visible underneath. A darker wet line lies above the remaining pool, leaving freshly exposed wood below it. The nearest varnished rim carries separate rounded liquid caps on the selected surface, each a small rain bead. Their curved contact boundaries meet the varnish, and there is surface texture visible between droplets in the exposed wood grain; a few thin rivulets follow the grain farther along the rim. From slightly above the gunwale in a front three-quarter view, the photograph includes her face, both working hands, the visible boat interior, the two hose endpoints and the receiving puddle in a single legible arrangement. The near rim stays large enough in the foreground for the individual rain beads and intervening grain to remain visibly resolved, while her face and working hands remain clear in the middle plane. Soft clearing daylight gives the water crisp local glints and the face gentle shape. Natural perspective and ample depth of field keep the water connections readable; the distant boats stay subordinate to her practical effort.
